author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The new test body contains a `for` loop iterating over `List.of("0", "-5")`. The brief (§ Test Structure) prohibits loops in test bodies and explicitly says to use `@ParameterizedTest` for repetitive cases. The [AUTOFIX] checklist category is 'Missing @ParameterizedTest for repetitive cases'. Convert to `@ParameterizedTest` with `@ValueSource(strings = {"0", "-5"})` and promote `page` to a method parameter.
findings.fix: Replace the for-loop with `@ParameterizedTest @ValueSource(strings = {"0", "-5"})` and add a `String page` parameter to the method signature. Each CSV row should stand on its own as a named case.

findings.description: Test name `processFindFormWithPageBelowOneReturnsFirstPage` violates the BDD naming school enforced from 2026-07-31 onward (brief § Test Naming: `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`). It names the production method (`processFindForm`) rather than the observable behavior, so it would not survive a production-method rename. Rename to something like `theOwnerListShouldRenderFirstPageWhenPageParamIsBelowOne`.
findings.fix: Rename the method to `theOwnerListShouldRenderFirstPageWhenPageParamIsBelowOne` (or equivalent `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` form).

findings.description: The test asserts HTTP 200 and the correct view name but does not verify that the repository was called with `pageNumber = 0`. A future regression that clamps to page index 1 instead of 0 (`Math.max(page - 1, 1)`) would still return HTTP 200 on the ownersList view and this test would pass. Add a `verify(owners).findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), argThat(p -> p.getPageNumber() == 0))` assertion (or equivalent) to pin that the first page is actually queried, not merely that no exception is thrown.
findings.fix: After the mockMvc assertions, add: `verify(owners, times(2)).findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), argThat(p -> p.getPageNumber() == 0));` — this confirms the clamping to page index 0, which is the core of the fix.

findings.description: The new test calls `new Owner()` directly inside the test body. The brief (§ Test Data Construction, applies from 2026-07-31 onward) requires: 'A slice adding a test writes it behind [a factory] from the start.' The bare `new Owner()` constructor is a Tier-2 value (irrelevant to the outcome) and should be hidden behind an anonymous factory such as `createAnOwner()`. The existing test `processFindFormSuccess` (pre-existing debt) has the same pattern; the new test should not replicate it.
findings.fix: Introduce a private `Owner createAnOwner()` factory method in the test class that returns a minimal, validly-populated Owner, and call it instead of `new Owner()` in the new test and in `processFindFormSuccess`.

approved_aspects: Production fix is minimal and correct: Math.max(page - 1, 0) in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName prevents the IllegalArgumentException PageRequest throws for negative page indices

HTTP 200 and ownersList view assertions do pin the primary regression: before the fix both inputs would have caused an exception and the response would not have been 200
Mocking policy is respected: MockMvc drives the real MVC dispatch while Mockito stubs the repository boundary, consistent with the project sanctioned pattern
Tests pass cleanly; the build and jacocoTestReport tasks succeed

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: addPaginationModel receives the raw page parameter (potentially 0 or negative) and stores it as the currentPage model attribute. The query is correctly clamped to the first page by findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, but the presentation layer sees the unclamped value. The ownersList.html template derives navigation URLs and page-button highlighting from currentPage: with page=0 no page number button is highlighted as current, and with page=-5 the next-page link URL resolves to ?page=-4, which silently re-clamps to page 1 on the next request. The fix addresses the repository layer but leaves the model attribute inconsistent.
findings.fix: Apply the clamp to the model attribute as well. Either compute int effectivePage = Math.max(page, 1) in processFindForm and pass it to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, or apply Math.max(page, 1) directly inside addPaginationModel when setting currentPage. The first option is cleaner because it keeps the semantic adjustment in one place and threads the normalized value consistently.

findings.description: The local variable Page<Owner> tasks names owner objects as task objects. The name belongs to a different domain concept and misleads the next reader about the contents of the page. This same defect appears pre-existing on lines 146, 165, 174, 188, and 200; the new test perpetuates it on line 153 rather than introducing a better name. Testing-principles.md three-tier naming applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward, which includes this new test.
findings.fix: Rename tasks to ownersPage on line 153.

findings.description: The test method is named processFindFormWithPageBelowOneReturnsFirstPage. Testing-principles.md § Test Naming (effective 2026-07-31) mandates the BDD school: the{Subject}Should{Outcome}. The current name identifies the production method being called rather than the behavior being specified, which means the name would not survive a production method rename. A new test written after the effective date must conform.
findings.fix: Rename to theOwnerListShouldReturnFirstPageWhenPageIsBelowOne or similar behavior-describing name.

findings.description: The test body contains a for-loop over List.of("0", "-5"). Testing-principles.md § Assertions linearity rule prohibits loops in test bodies and directs the use of collection-aware or parameterized constructs instead. The existing test processFindFormIgnoresSurroundingWhitespace (line 177) uses the same pattern and predates the rule; the new test is written after the 2026-07-31 effective date and must not replicate it.
findings.fix: Replace the for-loop with @ParameterizedTest and @ValueSource(strings = {"0", "-5"}), moving the mock setup into the test method body (or a per-invocation BeforeEach narrowing).
